extracted.intended_audience: lessees, grant holders, offshore wind developers, consultants, and other stakeholders subject to BOEM renewable energy plan and survey requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance and proposed rule provisions governing COP/FDR/FIR submittals, geophysical and geotechnical survey requirements and timing, CVA roles, fabrication/ procurement rules, and the renewable energy leasing schedule for offshore wind projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a Project Design Envelope (PDE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessee may submit a COP using a foundation PDE consisting of scenarios or ranges of design parameters or locations (e.g., all jacket foundations, all monopile foundations, half each). BOEM will assume the maximum design scenario (i.e., the scenario with the greatest impacts) for each affected resource in its environmental analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may approve the full PDE (giving lessees flexibility to construct using either or both foundation types) or approve only a subset if impacts of one type are unacceptable. BOEM supports voluntary use of the PDE and finds it beneficial because it provides latitude to make site-specific design and engineering decisions after plan approval without reopening permitting. Ranges may include non-design attributes such as installation methods or mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: COP requirement to include seabed and sub-seabed survey data
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM regulations require a lessee's COP to include survey data characterizing the seabed and sub-seabed that would be disturbed by the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These data inform BOEM's environmental analysis, statutory consultations (particularly historic resources and essential fish habitat), and technical feasibility review. Surveys are typically divided into geophysical (acoustic/magnetic mapping of seafloor, hazards, archaeological resources) and geotechnical (boreholes, vibracores, grab samplers to determine subsurface geology and identify potential archaeological resources). BOEM has guidelines elaborating best practices for such surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existing geotechnical survey content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Current regulations require geotechnical survey data to include results of a testing program investigating stratigraphic and engineering properties of sediment affecting foundations/anchoring; in situ testing, boring, and sampling at each foundation location; and at least one deep boring (with soil sampling/testing) at each edge of the project area and within the project area as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, lessees are currently obligated to conduct a full suite of geotechnical surveys before COP submittal. Lessees must apply for a regulatory departure under §585.103 if they wish to defer in situ testing, boring, and sampling at each foundation location until the FDR stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: COP must include results of archaeological resource survey with supporting data
rubrics_metrics.description: A lessee's COP is required to include 'the results of the archaeological resource survey with supporting data.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM therefore requires the results of all archaeological surveys to be submitted with the COP, though the proposed rule contemplates allowing some subsea archaeological surveys to be deferred to the FDR on a case-by-case basis subject to terms and conditions of COP approval (recognizing potential NHPA section 106 consultation timing risks).

rubrics_metrics.name: COP sufficiency review and baseline geological information
rubrics_metrics.description: The COP must contain information sufficient to define the baseline geological conditions of the seabed, develop a geologic model, assess geologic hazards, and determine the feasibility of the proposed site for the proposed facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM conducts a COP sufficiency review after receipt of a COP and notifies lessees of information shortfalls that must be filled before COP review is complete. The COP must contain information necessary to conduct required consultations and authorizations of other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shift from prescriptive to performance-based COP survey standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would shift survey and data collection requirements from largely prescriptive standards to performance-based standards for 'geological and geotechnical' topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance-based standards give lessees leeway to demonstrate that their selected combination of geotechnical and geophysical surveys provide BOEM the data it needs at the COP review stage to determine whether the project as designed can be constructed safely in the proposed range of locations—so long as industry standard engineering practices are used at subsequent phases. Lessees could strike their own balance between geotechnical and geophysical surveys at the COP stage, subject to BOEM deeming the data sufficient for BOEM's review and required consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow staged data collection and deferred geotechnical submittal to FDR
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would allow submission of certain geophysical and geotechnical data and analysis in stages and permit submission of geotechnical data for engineering assessment with a lessee's FDR rather than requiring all in situ borings at COP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staged collection mirrors European and industry practices and accommodates technology evolution, reduces re-surveying when exact turbine locations change, and may lower costs/delays. Deferred data would be subject to terms and conditions of COP approval and BOEM's sufficiency review to ensure environmental and consultation needs are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM authority to require COP revision or halt activities if deferred data inconsistent
rubrics_metrics.description: If deferred geotechnical or archaeological survey data reveal impacts or conflicts not considered previously, BOEM may require the lessee to revise the COP under §585.634 or halt/require modifications to deferred surveys/activities under lease suspension authority at §585.417(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any deferred data would be subject to terms and conditions of COP approval allowing the Department to stop or require modification of further activities if data are inconsistent with COP analysis. The Department retains authority to ensure safety and environmental protection prior to installation.

rubrics_metrics.name: COP-level data sufficient for interagency consultations while engineering details may be deferred
rubrics_metrics.description: The COP must still contain non-geotechnical survey data sufficient to assess impacts to the human, marine, and coastal environment, conduct necessary statutory consultations, and show technical feasibility of proposed foundation types, while detailed engineering geotechnical data may be deferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM's oil and gas program uses a similar approach (non-geotechnical at plan stage; geotechnical after plan approval). Historical experience (2,600 oil and gas plan approvals) is cited to support that deferred geotechnical surveys have not required EIS supplementation or reinitiation of consultation in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicited potential survey-permit and reporting requirements (questions for comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM solicits comments on whether additional protections should be adopted via rulemaking that cannot be achieved by lease stipulations, including whether BOEM should establish a permit-based mechanism for surveys, improve reporting/reimbursement procedures, require additional public reporting/notice beyond two weeks, track OCS survey activities, and require advance coordination with other lessees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific questions include: Should BOEM establish a permit-based mechanism for how/when/where surveys are conducted? Should there be methods other than permits to confirm damage to fishing gear and identify responsible parties? To what extent should BOEM require additional public reporting and notice of anticipated survey activities? How can BOEM improve reporting and reimbursement procedures for harmed parties? Are there other policies to minimize adverse interactions between other OCS users and surveyors?

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified Verification Agent (CVA) verification role and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The CVA is required as an independent third-party to provide verification (not 'certification') of a project's FDR and FIR, verify the facility's design taking human safety into appropriate consideration, evaluate commissioning of any critical safety systems, monitor fabrication and installation activities, and submit a final report to BOEM before the start of commercial operations or other approved activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule changes terminology from 'certification' to 'verification' to align with industry standards. Critical safety systems are defined as systems/equipment designed to prevent or ameliorate major accidents that could result in harm to health, safety, or the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in CVA nomination and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would decouple CVA nomination and approval from plan (SAP, COP, or GAP) submittal and approval, allowing lessees/grant holders to have approved CVAs in place earlier and to nominate new or replacement CVAs as projects progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessees may nominate separate CVAs to review different components of a project. Early CVA involvement is encouraged to support safety and best engineering practices and to provide third-party review of design concepts before plan submittal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staged submittal of Facility Design Reports (FDR) and Fabrication and Installation Reports (FIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would clarify and permit staged submission of FDRs and FIRs for discrete major project components, rather than requiring a single FDR/FIR for the entire project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staged submittals would be allowed only if the lessee or grant holder can (1) explain how the constituent major components would function together in an integrated manner and (2) demonstrate that a CVA has verified such integration. These qualifications aim to minimize risks of having to modify completed fabrications or installations due to later-reviewed components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'fabrication' and early off‑OCS fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposes to define 'fabrication' as 'cutting, fitting, welding or other assembly of project elements of a custom design conforming to project-specific requirements' and to exclude procurement of discrete standardized/commercially available parts and type-certified components (e.g., nacelles, blades) from that definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation is clarified to prohibit only fabrication and installation that take place on the OCS prior to BOEM non-objection; fabrication activities that do not take place on the OCS may commence prior to submittal of the FDR, FIR, or plans, and do not require prior issuance of a departure. However, BOEM reserves the right to object to installation of previously fabricated/procured components if inconsistent with industry/engineering standards, approved plans, or the FDR/FIR. Lessee assumes business risk for off-OCS fabrication prior to BOEM non-objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA verification requirement applies to all procured or fabricated components
rubrics_metrics.description: All facility components procured or fabricated, regardless of where they were fabricated (on- or off-OCS), would be subject to CVA verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces risk of cost-saving procurement/fabrication choices undermining safety or engineering practices; BOEM can still object to installations inconsistent with standards or approved plans during FDR/FIR reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewable Energy Leasing Schedule publication and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would add a new section requiring BOEM to publish a proposed five-year renewable energy leasing schedule and periodic updates to that schedule (at least once every two years), including locations under consideration, calendar year of projected lease sales, and reasons for changes to prior schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a proposed schedule it would not obligate BOEM to offer all sales listed; BOEM would adjust the schedule as necessary. The first schedule would be for the five-year period following the rule's effective date, with subsequent schedules covering the five-year period after each update; updates would identify lease sales being considered for the following five-year period to provide transparency and facilitate planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) leasing constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will comply with IRA (Public Law 117-169) requirements that, during the 10-year period beginning August 16, 2022, BOEM may not issue an OCS wind lease unless an OCS oil and gas lease sale has been held during the 1-year period ending on the date of issuance of the wind lease and the sum total of acres offered in such oil and gas lease sales during that 1-year period is at least 60 million acres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory constraint will affect timing/availability of wind lease issuances and is part of the context for the renewable energy leasing schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of departures and regulatory tools to manage timing conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lessee wishes to deviate from existing pre‑COP in situ testing/boring requirements, they must apply for a regulatory departure under §585.103; BOEM has granted departures on a case‑by‑case basis, typically conditioning them on lessee assumption of business risk and reserving BOEM's right to object later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule reduces need for frequent departure requests by clarifying flexibility (e.g., off‑OCS fabrication permitted), but departures remain the mechanism when exceptions to standard timing are sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged early coordination with relevant agencies on site characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM could recommend, as a best practice, that developers coordinate early with relevant agencies on applicable site characterization plans before surveys occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early coordination may reduce risks of consultation delays (e.g., NHPA section 106) and help ensure survey plans will meet BOEM and other agencies' information needs.
